newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC says likely to drop Vietnam oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC says likely to drop Vietnam oil refinery.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp is considering withdrawing from plans to invest in a U$1.6 billion refinery project in Vietnam due to its likely low return, executives said on Monday.
"Chinese Petroleum reviewed the Vietnam refinery project and is likely to stop the plan due to its low investment return," a company official told Reuters by telephone.
The outlook for a low return resulted from the Vietnamese government's unwillingness to offer favorable treatment to the project, the official said.
Chinese Petroleum wants a 15 percent return on investment for the project, but a company review showed an expected return of less than half that, the official said.
The US$1.6 billion Dung Quat oil refinery, with a capacity of 6.5 million tonnes per year, would be located in the central province of Quang Ngai.
The area is undeveloped and far from Vietnam's offshore fields and major oil consuming areas.
Under existing plans, Chinese Petroleum and Taiwan's Chinese Investment Development Corp would together have taken 10 percent in the consortium developing the project.

Other partners include Petrovietnam with a 30 percent stake, South Korea's LG Group with 27 percent, Stone & Webster with three percent, and Malaysia's Petronas and U.S. refiner Conoco split a 30 percent equally.
Conoco is a unit of DuPont Co.

The official said Petronas and Conoco also were likely to withdraw their investment for the same reason, but LG Group and Stone & Webster had no plans to back out of what could be a lucrative construction project.
"LG and Stone Webster are likely to stay on the plan and are seeking the refinery project's construction contract," the official said.
The French oil firm Total SA withdrew from the refinery project in 1995, calling it economically unviable.
Vietnam has no major oil refinery and refined oil product demand is booming due to economic reforms.
